  • TREMFYA showed statistically significant improvement in disease activity on the BASDAI score versus placebo, reflecting meaningful reductions in pain, stiffness, swelling and fatigue in a Phase 4 study
  • TREMFYA demonstrated more than 2 times greater reduction in MRI-assessed inflammation versus placebo at Week 24 in the sacroiliac joints, which connect the lower spine to the pelvis and are responsible for pain and stiffness
  • TREMFYA was evaluated in first-ever PsA study using objective MRI assessments to confirm and measure axial inflammation alongside patient-reported symptoms

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) today announced late-breaking results from the Phase 4 STAR study of TREMFYA (guselkumab) in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis and axial involvement (axial PsA). TREMFYA met primary and major secondary endpoints that demonstrated significant improvement in axial symptoms compared to placebo and significant reduction of MRI-assessed inflammation in the sacroiliac joints.1,a The Phase 4 STAR study is the first and only dedicated randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to prospectively evaluate an IL-23 inhibitor specifically in patients with axial involvement in PsA confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The late-breaking results are being presented at the Emirates Society for Rheumatology (ESR) Annual Meeting.

For people living with psoriatic arthritis, axial involvement can add another layer of burden to an already complex disease. Chronic inflammation of the spine and sacroiliac joints can cause back pain and stiffness, limiting patients' mobility and physical function.2 Axial involvement may affect approximately 5 to 28 percent of patients with early PsA and 25 to 70 percent of those with longer-standing disease.13 Despite advances in treatment, axial PsA remains challenging to classify, and very few prospective clinical trials have been dedicated specifically to this patient population, underscoring the urgent need for more robust evidence in this subset of PsA patients.

"Axial involvement in psoriatic arthritis can be difficult to identify and evaluate, leaving clinicians with limited evidence to guide patient selection for clinical trials and possibly treatment decisions," said Prof. Mikkel Ostergaard, M.D., Ph.D., DMSc, Clinical Professor of Rheumatology at the University of Copenhagen and Consultant in Rheumatology and Chairperson of the Copenhagen Center for Arthritis Research (COPECARE) at the Center for Rheumatology and Spine Diseases, Rigshospitalet, Glostrup.f "In the STAR study, TREMFYA showed significant improvements in patient-reported symptoms and MRI-assessed axial inflammation in the sacroiliac joints, backed by a well-characterized safety profile. Together, these findings provide important evidence to help inform treatment decisions for this debilitating and understudied manifestation of psoriatic arthritis."

TREMFYA demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements, reflecting reductions across patient-reported domains including spinal pain, stiffness, fatigue, joint symptoms and areas of tenderness. At Week 24, mean Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI)b scores, which are on a 10-point scale, improved by −3.3 with TREMFYA 100 mg every four weeks (Q4W) and −2.9 with TREMFYA every eight weeks (Q8W) versus −2.1 with placebo.1,c

TREMFYA Q4Wc and Q8W also demonstrated significant improvements in symptoms, as measured by the Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score using C-reactive protein (ASDAS-CRP)d compared with placebo at Week 24 (−1.5 and −1.3, respectively, versus −0.8).1 These exceeded the internationally recognized standard of ≥1.1 units for clinically important improvement, reflecting a reduction in C-reactive protein, a marker of inflammation in the body.3

TREMFYA also provided high levels of skin clearance in patients treated with TREMFYA Q4W and Q8W, consistent with skin clearance demonstrated in other PsA studies such as DISCOVER I and II and APEX.4 5 6 Additionally, the overall safety profile observed in the STAR study was consistent with the established safety profile of TREMFYA in psoriatic disease, and no new safety signals were identified.1

The notable measure in this study was MRI-assessed sacroiliac joint inflammation, measured using the Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada (SPARCC)e score. TREMFYA reduced scores by −7.1 and −5.2, with Q4W and Q8W, respectively, versus −2.4 with placebo, representing more than 2 times greater improvement than placebo.1

"Psoriatic arthritis is a complex disease that can affect patients in many ways, from skin and peripheral joint symptoms to irreversible joint damage to axial involvement," said David M. Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Global Immunology Therapeutic Area Head, Johnson & Johnson. "The STAR study brings new insight to axial PsA research showing that TREMFYA can improve axial symptoms and MRI-detected inflammation, while uniquely establishing evidence for an IL-23 inhibitor. Johnson & Johnson continues to pioneer new studies to challenge norms for patients, and these results further reinforce the role of TREMFYA in addressing the diverse manifestations of psoriatic arthritis."

Editor's notes:

a. The change from baseline in Health Assessment Questionnaire - Disability Index (HAQ-DI) was numerically greater for Q8W dosing but did not achieve statistical significance.
b. BASDAI is a validated patient-reported outcome (PRO) originally developed to measure disease activity on a 0 to 10 scale in ankylosing spondylitis (AS), now referred to as radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA).7
c. TREMFYA is not approved for Q4W dosing in the U.S.
d. ASDAS-CRP, or Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score with C-Reactive Protein, is a validated, composite index that combines patient-reported symptoms with a laboratory biomarker to objectively measure inflammation and disease severity.8 9
e. The Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada (SPARCC) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) score is a validated, objective, semiquantitative scoring system used to measure active inflammatory changes in the spine and sacroiliac joint.10
f. Prof. Ostergaard is a paid consultant for Johnson & Johnson. He has not been compensated for any media work.

About the STAR study (NCT04929210)

STAR is a Phase 4, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating TREMFYA in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis and axial disease. Eligible participants had active PsA with objective evidence of axial inflammation confirmed by centrally read MRI and elevated C-reactive protein despite previous treatment with non-biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), apremilast and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).11

The study enrolled 411 participants worldwide and includes a 24-week placebo-controlled treatment period followed by a 24-week active treatment period. The primary endpoint evaluated change from baseline in the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) at Week 24. Secondary endpoints include additional assessments of axial disease activity, MRI inflammation, physical function, peripheral musculoskeletal manifestations, skin disease and safety.11

About psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement

Psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement (axial PsA) is a chronic inflammatory condition where psoriatic arthritis affects the spine and sacroiliac joints (connecting the lower spine to the pelvis). It can cause inflammatory back pain, neck stiffness, and reduced mobility, in addition to the joint, skin or nail manifestations commonly associated with PsA.12 13

Despite significant advances in the treatment of psoriatic arthritis, axial involvement remains an area of substantial ongoing need and research.14 While it shares some clinical features with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), axial involvement is increasingly recognized as a distinct domain of psoriatic arthritis.15 However, there is currently no universally accepted definition or validated classification criteria specific to PsA with axial involvement, and prospective studies conducted exclusively in patients with axial involvement remain very limited.16

About TREMFYA (guselkumab)

Developed by Johnson & Johnson, TREMFYA is the first approved fully-human, dual-acting monoclonal antibody designed to neutralize inflammation at the cellular source by blocking IL-23 and binding to CD64 (a receptor on cells that produce IL-23). Findings for dual-acting are limited to in vitro studies that demonstrate guselkumab binds to CD64, which is expressed on the surface of IL-23 producing cells in an inflammatory monocyte model. The clinical significance of this finding is not known.

TREMFYA is a prescription medicine approved in the U.S. to treat:

  • adults and children six years and older who also weigh at least 40 kg with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or phototherapy (treatment using ultraviolet or UV light).
  • adults and children six years and older who also weigh at least 40 kg with active psoriatic arthritis.
  • adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
  • adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.

TREMFYA is approved in Europe, Canada, Japan, and a number of other countries for the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, adults with active psoriatic arthritis, adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease and adults with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

The manufacturer for TREMFYA is Janssen Biotech, Inc.

Johnson & Johnson maintains exclusive worldwide marketing rights to TREMFYA. For more information, visit: www.tremfya.com.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?

TREMFYA is a prescription medicine that may cause serious side effects, including:

  • Serious Allergic Reactions. Stop using TREMFYA and get emergency medical help right away if you develop any of the following symptoms of a serious allergic reaction:

o fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)

o swelling of your face, eyelids, lips, mouth, tongue or throat

o trouble breathing or throat tightness

o chest tightness

o skin rash, hives

o itching

  • Infections. TREMFYA may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider should check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment with TREMFYA and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with TREMFYA if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with TREMFYA.

Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:

o fever, sweats, or chills

o muscle aches

o weight loss

o cough

o warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis

o diarrhea or stomach pain

o shortness of breath

o blood in your phlegm (mucus)

o burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

  • Liver problems. With the treatment of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, your healthcare provider will do blood tests to check your liver before and during treatment with TREMFYA. With the treatment of plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis, your healthcare provider may do blood tests to check your liver before and as necessary during treatment with TREMFYA. Your healthcare provider may stop treatment with TREMFYA if you develop liver problems. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you notice any of the following symptoms:

o unexplained rash

o vomiting

o tiredness (fatigue)

o yellowing of the skin or the whites of your eyes

o nausea

o stomach pain (abdominal)

o loss of appetite

o dark urine

Do not use TREMFYA if you have had a serious allergic reaction to guselkumab or any of the ingredients in TREMFYA.

Before using TREMFYA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?"
  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.
  • have TB or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). You should avoid receiving live vaccines during treatment with TREMFYA. Children should be brought up to date with all vaccines before starting TREMFYA
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if TREMFYA can harm your unborn baby.
    Pregnancy Registry: If you become pregnant during treatment with TREMFYA, talk to your healthcare provider about registering in the pregnancy exposure registry for TREMFYA. You can enroll by visiting www.mothertobaby.org/ongoing-study/tremfya-guselkumab, by calling 1-877-311-8972, or emailing MotherToBaby@health.ucsd.edu. The purpose of this registry is to collect information about the safety of TREMFYA during pregnancy.
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if TREMFYA passes into your breast milk.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

What are the possible side effects of TREMFYA?

TREMFYA may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?"

The most common side effects of TREMFYA include: respiratory tract infections, headache, injection site reactions, joint pain (arthralgia), diarrhea, stomach flu (gastroenteritis), fungal skin infections, herpes simplex infections, stomach pain, bronchitis, feeling very tired (fatigue), fever (pyrexia), and skin rash.

These are not all the possible side effects of TREMFYA. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use TREMFYA exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to use it.

Please read the full Prescribing Information, including Medication Guide, for TREMFYA and discuss any questions that you have with your doctor.

You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

Dosage Forms and Strengths: TREMFYA is available as 100 mg/mL and 200 mg/2mL for subcutaneous injection and as a 200 mg/20 mL (10 mg/mL) single dose vial for intravenous infusion.

Global, social-first campaign gives well-known hosts the chance to be guests themselves, with locally inspired creative, new consumer research and bookable experiences

ATLANTA, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- It's time to leave "host mode" at home. New data from IHG Hotels & Resorts finds that two-thirds of travelers who often play the role of host among family and friends say organizing a trip can feel like another job, and they're ready to swap the to-do list for being taken care of.

Enter "When the Host Needs Hosting," IHG's global, social-first campaign rooted in the idea that even the best hosts deserve to be hosted. Across the United States, Mexico, Australia, Japan, the United Kingdom and Germany, the campaign features some of the world's most beloved personalities taking a break from their usual host roles to experience IHG hospitality firsthand, this time as a guest.

"At IHG, we know a lot about what it means to be a great host, and how much thought goes into making someone feel truly welcome," said Connor Smith, Senior Vice President of Global Brands – Luxury, Lifestyle, Masterbrand and Global Creative Director. "With a portfolio of 21 hotel brands spanning over 100 countries around the world, we have the opportunity to create meaningful experiences that make every guest feel genuinely cared for. 'When the Host Needs Hosting' is a reminder that great hospitality is about more than where you stay. It's about how you feel while you're there."

While united by a global theme, each market brings its own perspective to the campaign, drawing on local personalities, cultural insights and new research* to explore what hosting and being hosted means around the world.

United States
Kicking off in the U.S., comedian, media personality and celebrity interviewer, Amelia Dimoldenberg trades her usual role as a host for a well-earned stay offering a playful look at what happens when the person asking all the questions finally gets to switch off. The collaboration also inspired "Hosted Like a Host," a limited-time bookable hotel experience bringing Dimoldenberg's favorite ways to travel, unwind and indulge to select IHG hotels.

Mexico 
In Mexico, television host, model and entrepreneur Montserrat Oliver brings "Viajar a la Mexicana" to life, celebrating the warmth, spontaneity and joyful spirit of Mexican travel and hospitality. Rooted in a culture where making others feel welcome and cared for comes naturally, the campaign gives Oliver a chance to experience that same hospitality herself after more than three decades of hosting.

Australia
Australians spend an estimated 478 million hours each year planning, preparing, hosting and cleaning up after get-togethers, according to new research from IHG and YouGov. In celebration of the country's everyday hosts, IHG partnered with celebrity chef and TV host Melissa Leong to turn the tables on hosting, inviting her to step out of the kitchen and into the guest suite. The campaign continues on-property with five limited-time hotel experiences inspired by Melissa Leong's own hosting style, available for IHG One Rewards members to bid on using points through Nov. 20, 2026 (or later).  

Japan
In Japan, local research offers another perspective on hosting: those who regularly care for others often find joy in doing so, while also valuing opportunities to relax on their own terms. Actor and artist Dean Fujioka brings that insight to life in "When the Host Needs Hosting: Travel, Your Way," exploring two distinct stays through Hotel Indigo's connection to local neighborhoods and Kimpton's personalized approach to hospitality. IHG One Rewards members can also access behind-the-scenes footage and an interview with Fujioka about his personal travel preferences.

U.K.
In the U.K., new research from IHG and OnePoll revealed that nearly six in ten (58%) people who regularly take care of others and organize group plans find themselves carrying those responsibilities with them when they go away. TV presenter Josie Gibson puts that insight at the heart of her hotel stays, handing over the planning and embracing a trip where someone else takes care of the details. PRINCETON, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CytoSorbents Corporation (NASDAQ: CTSO, the "Company"), a leader in the treatment of life-threatening conditions in the intensive care unit and cardiac surgery using blood purification, today announced a $6.25 million common stock financing.

CytoSorbents Secures $6.25M At-Market Financing, Cuts Debt by $5.25M, and Extends Debt Maturity to 2028

Registered Direct Offering

The Company has entered into securities purchase agreements with certain institutional and accredited investors and certain insiders of the Company for the issuance and sale in a registered direct offering (the "Offering") priced at-the-market under Nasdaq rules of (i) an aggregate of 556,681 shares (the "Common Shares") of the Company's common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the "Common Stock"), at a purchase price of $4.94 per share, and 96,527 shares of Common Stock to the Company's directors and certain executive officers at an offering price of $5.18 per share, which was the consolidated closing bid price of our Common Stock on The Nasdaq Capital Market on November 18, 2026, and (ii) pre-funded warrants (the "Pre-Funded Warrants") to purchase up to an aggregate of 151,822 shares of Common Stock (the "Pre-Funded Warrant Shares," together with the Common Shares, the "Shares"), at a purchase price of $4.939 per Pre-Funded Warrant, equal to the purchase price per Common Share less $0.001. Each Pre-Funded Warrant is immediately exercisable for one share of Common Stock at an exercise price of $0.001 per Pre-Funded Warrant Share until such Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised in full.

The Offering is expected to consist of approximately $4.0 million of gross cash proceeds, with approximately 75% of the Offering subscribed for by existing shareholders and members of the Company's management and Board of Directors.

H.C. Wainwright & Co. is acting as exclusive placement agent for the Offering.  WBB Securities, LLC is acting as financial advisor in connection with the Offering.

The Offering is expected to close on or about November 20, 2026, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions. Gross proceeds from the Offering are expected to be approximately $4.0 million, before deducting placement agent fees, financial advisor fees and offering expenses payable by the Company. The Company intends to use the net proceeds for (i) the repayment of $3.0 million of outstanding principal under its existing loan agreement with Avenue Capital Group ("Avenue"), together with a $52,500 prepayment fee and a $270,000 final payment, and (ii) general corporate and working capital purposes.

Avenue Credit Facility Amendment

Concurrently with the Offering, the Company entered into the Third Amendment to Loan Documents (the "Avenue Amendment"), dated November 19, 2026, to its existing Loan and Security Agreement dated June 28, 2024, as amended, with Avenue. 

Key terms include:

  • Debt reduction of $5.25 million:  Repayment of $3.0 million of principal in cash from the Offering proceeds, plus a $52,500 prepayment fee and a $270,000 final payment, and satisfaction of $2.25 million of principal through the issuance of 455,465 shares of Common Stock to Avenue Venture Opportunities Fund, L.P. at the Offering price of $4.94 per share. Following these transactions, $12.25 million of principal will remain outstanding, down from $17.5 million. The Company expects to save approximately $0.7 million in interest expense over 12 months.
  • Maturity extended one year:  The maturity date is extended from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2028.
  • Interest-only period extended 15 months:  Interest-only payments are extended through March 31, 2028, with a further three-month extension available if the Company has received FDA marketing approval for DrugSorb-ATR by that date, subject to other conditions.
  • New conversion rights:  Avenue's existing $2.0 million conversion right is replaced with the right to convert (i) up to $3.0 million of principal into Common Stock at $6.916 per share, equal to 140% of the $4.94 Offering price, exercisable at any time, and (ii) up to an additional $3.125 million of principal at $8.645 per share, equal to 175% of the Offering price, exercisable beginning on the earlier of FDA marketing approval of DrugSorb-ATR and January 1, 2028. Any conversion would further reduce the Company's outstanding debt.
  • Other terms: The Avenue Amendment also modifies certain beneficial ownership limitations and financial covenants, provides certain registration rights and provides for a back-end fee of $250,000, payable on July 1, 2028 (or earlier repayment) and waived if Avenue achieves a net profit of at least 300% on the initial $2.25 million repayment shares.

Of the shares issued to Avenue in satisfaction of $2.25 million of principal, shares satisfying $1.0 million of principal (the "Registered Shares") will be issued pursuant to the Company's effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-281062), and shares satisfying the remaining $1.25 million of principal will be issued in a transaction exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The shares issued to Avenue are in addition to the securities issued in the Offering and will not generate additional cash proceeds to the Company. The cash repayment and issuance of shares to Avenue in satisfaction of the Company's indebtedness are expected to occur substantially concurrently with the closing of the Offering, subject to applicable closing conditions. 

Registration and Offering Information

The Common Shares, Pre-Funded Warrants, Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and Registered Shares are being offered and sold pursuant to a "shelf" registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-281062), which was declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on September 30, 2024. The Offering is being made only by means of a prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus forming part of the effective registration statement. A final prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus relating to the Offering and the Registered Shares will be filed with the SEC. Electronic copies may be obtained, when available, on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov or by contacting H.C. Wainwright & Co., LLC, 430 Park Avenue, 3rd Floor, New York, New York 10022, at placements@hcwco.com or (212) 856-5711.

The shares issued to Avenue in satisfaction of the remaining $1.25 million of principal are being issued in a transaction not involving a public offering and have not been registered under the Securities Act or applicable state securities laws. Such shares may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. The Company has agreed to file a registration statement with the SEC covering the resale of these shares.

This press release shall not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any of the securities described herein, and there shall not be any offer, solicitation or sale of such securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction.

About CytoSorbents Corporation (NASDAQ: CTSO)

CytoSorbents Corporation is a leader in the treatment of life-threatening conditions in the intensive care unit and cardiac surgery through blood purification. CytoSorbents' proprietary blood purification technologies are based on biocompatible, highly porous polymer beads that can actively remove toxic substances from blood and other bodily fluids by pore capture and surface adsorption. Cartridges filled with these beads can be used with standard blood pumps already in the hospital (e.g. dialysis, continuous renal replacement therapy or CRRT, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or ECMO, and heart-lung machines), where blood is repeatedly recirculated outside the body, through our cartridges where toxic substances are removed, and then back into the body. CytoSorbents' technologies are used in a number of broad applications. Specifically, two important applications are 1) the removal of blood thinners during and after cardiothoracic surgery to reduce the risk of severe bleeding, and 2) the removal of inflammatory agents and toxins in common critical illnesses that can lead to massive inflammation, organ failure and patient death. The breadth of these critical illnesses includes, for example, sepsis, burn injury, trauma, lung injury, liver failure, cytokine release syndrome, and pancreatitis as well as the removal of liver toxins that accumulate in acute liver dysfunction or failure, and the removal of myoglobin in severe rhabdomyolysis that can otherwise lead to renal failure. In these diseases, the risk of death can be extremely high, and there are few, if any, effective treatments.

CytoSorbents' lead product, CytoSorb®, is approved in the European Union and distributed in over 70 countries worldwide, with more than 300,000 devices used cumulatively to date. CytoSorb was originally launched in the European Union under CE mark as the first cytokine adsorber. Additional CE mark extensions were granted for bilirubin and myoglobin removal in clinical conditions such as liver disease and trauma, respectively, and for ticagrelor and rivaroxaban removal in cardiothoracic surgery procedures. CytoSorb has also received FDA Emergency Use Authorization in the United States for use in adult critically ill COVID-19 patients with impending or confirmed respiratory failure. CytoSorb is not yet approved or cleared in the United States.

In the U.S. and Canada, CytoSorbents is developing the DrugSorb™-ATR antithrombotic removal system, an investigational device based on an equivalent polymer technology to CytoSorb, to reduce the severity of perioperative bleeding in high-risk surgery due to blood thinning drugs. It has received two FDA Breakthrough Device Designations: one for the removal of ticagrelor and another for the removal of the direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) apixaban and rivaroxaban in a cardiopulmonary bypass circuit during urgent cardiothoracic surgery. The Company is actively pursuing regulatory approval of DrugSorb-ATR with the U.S. FDA and will pursue regulatory approval with Health Canada with better visibility from the FDA. DrugSorb-ATR is not yet granted or approved in either the U.S. or Canada.

The Company has numerous marketed products and products under development based upon this unique blood purification technology protected by many issued U.S. and international patents and registered trademarks, and multiple patent applications pending, including ECOS-300CY®, CytoSorb-XL™, HemoDefend-RBC™, HemoDefend-BGA™, VetResQ®, K+ontrol™, DrugSorb™, ContrastSorb, PuriFi®, HotSwap®, and others. Company's 16-Qubit Algorithm Produces Results Advancing the Potential for More Computationally Efficient Nuclear Modeling

TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quantum X Labs (the "Company" or "QXL"), a developer of advanced quantum computing technologies, today announced a technological milestone achieved by its Nuclear Simulation Team, successfully executing a quantum algorithm designed to simulate photon transport through shielding materials on IBM's Fez superconducting quantum processor.

The experiment demonstrated the ability of a 16-qubit quantum algorithm to accurately reproduce key characteristics of photon propagation, scattering, attenuation and detection through a two-dimensional tungsten collimator, producing results closely aligned with analytical calculations and classical simulations.

Beyond demonstrating accuracy, the significance of the experiment lies in the potential of quantum algorithms to reduce the computational resources required for complex nuclear simulations.

Conventional GPU-based Monte Carlo simulations rely on processing large numbers of individual particle histories to calculate radiation behavior, often requiring substantial computational resources. Quantum X Labs is developing an alternative approach that uses quantum-state preparation and reversible quantum operations to encode particle transport probabilities and evaluate detection outcomes.

In the experiment, each measurement point was evaluated using 4,096 quantum shots, with results closely matching classical references. The demonstrated circuit provides a foundation for future quantum amplitude estimation, which could reduce the sampling effort needed to estimate radiation transport probabilities. The experiment did not implement amplitude estimation or establish an efficiency advantage over GPU-based methods.

The experiment simulated the transport of 140 keV photons through a tungsten collimator, evaluating the effects of shielding attenuation, channel geometry and detector energy thresholds.

Following hardware-noise mitigation, the quantum algorithm demonstrated:

  • High accuracy: Root-mean-square deviations of approximately 0.03–0.04 compared with exact classical statevector simulation results.
  • Successful radiation modeling: Accurate reproduction of changes in photon detection probability resulting from variations in tungsten attenuation and channel width.
  • Real quantum hardware validation: Successful execution of the 16-qubit algorithm on IBM's Fez superconducting quantum processor.

"What makes this achievement important is not simply that our quantum algorithm reproduced classical simulation results, but that we demonstrated a coherent and efficient oracle that can serve as a foundation for quantum amplitude estimation," said David Shnaiderov, Head of Nuclear Quantum at Quantum X Labs. "Conventional GPU-based methods can require large numbers of particle histories. Our next objective is to integrate amplitude estimation and test whether it can deliver comparable accuracy with fewer sampling operations. Demonstrating the underlying circuit on real quantum hardware is an important step toward that goal."

Radiation transport simulation plays an important role across the nuclear energy, aerospace, defense, medical imaging and radiation shielding industries. More computationally efficient simulation methods could support increasingly complex system designs while potentially reducing computational requirements.

Quantum X Labs intends to expand the complexity of its nuclear simulation algorithms, integrate quantum amplitude estimation with the demonstrated oracle, and benchmark sampling requirements and computational performance against GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods.

EAST AURORA, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Moog Inc. (NYSE: MOG.A and MOG.B), a worldwide designer, manufacturer and systems integrator of high-performance precision motion and fluid controls and control systems, today reported record fiscal 2026 results for sales, adjusted segment operating margin, adjusted diluted net earnings per share and free cash flow, along with a strong fiscal fourth quarter.

“Fiscal 2026 was a milestone year for the company. We delivered record results and achieved the goals we established at our 2023 Investor Day," said Pat Roche, CEO. "These results reflect our employees' dedication to improving how we operate and better serving our customers. I'm proud of what we accomplished in our 75th anniversary year and confident in our ability to deliver sustained, profitable growth and long-term value creation."

Quarter Highlights

  • Record quarter net sales in all four segments.
  • Segment operating margin increased due to the absence of the prior year's legal settlement charges, the current quarter's gain on the sale of a non-core business and stronger business performance.
  • Adjusted segment operating margin increased due to stronger business performance.
  • Increases in diluted net earnings per share and adjusted diluted net earnings per share were primarily driven by business performance.
  • Free cash flow generation decreased due to a greater use of working capital.
  • Twelve-month backlog increased 14% to $3.4 billion, reflecting continued demand across all markets.

Year Highlights

  • Record annual net sales, reflecting strength across all four segments.
  • Segment operating margin benefitted from lower simplification and other charges, $30 million of refund claims related to previously incurred International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") tariffs and stronger business performance.
  • Adjusted segment operating margin increased 70 basis points due to the tariff refund and 50 basis points due to stronger business performance.
  • Diluted net earnings per share increased significantly due to stronger business performance and income tax benefits attributable to current and prior fiscal years.
  • Adjusted diluted net earnings per share was driven by stronger business performance.
  • Free cash flow improved, reflecting higher earnings as well as effective management of working capital.

Quarter Segment Results

Sales in the fourth quarter of 2026 were $1.3 billion, an increase of 20% compared to the fourth quarter of 2025. Space and Defense sales increased 27% to $389 million, reflecting broad-based defense demand including demand for missile controls and for spacecraft components. Military Aircraft sales increased 20% to $283 million, driven by higher OEM activity on production and funded development programs. Commercial Aircraft sales increased 13% to $286 million, driven by growth in aftermarket and higher OEM production levels. Industrial sales increased 17% to $297 million, driven by strong demand for data center cooling pumps, as well as the timing of medical orders.

Segment operating margin in the fourth quarter of 2026 was 14.2%, an increase of 230 basis points compared to the fourth quarter of 2025. Space and Defense operating margin increased 340 basis points to 13.6% due to the absence of the prior year's legal settlement charges. Industrial operating margin increased 190 basis points to 14.6% due to the efficiencies from scaling to meet higher demand for data center cooling pumps. Military Aircraft operating margin increased 170 basis points to 15.7% driven by pricing and favorable mix. Commercial Aircraft operating margin increased 150 basis points to 12.9% due to the gain on the sale of a non-core business.

Adjusted segment operating margin in the fourth quarter of 2026 expanded 40 basis points to 14.1% compared to the fourth quarter of 2025. The fourth quarter of 2025 adjusted segment operating margin excludes $18 million of charges, primarily related to the legal settlement. Space and Defense adjusted margin decreased 140 basis points to 13.7% as increased product development, business capture and operational readiness investments were partially offset by profitable sales growth. Commercial Aircraft adjusted margin decreased 50 basis points to 10.9% due to an unfavorable sales mix. Adjusted segment operating margins in Industrial and Military Aircraft increased 240 basis points and 160 basis points, respectively.

Year Segment Results

Sales for fiscal 2026 were $4.5 billion, an increase of 17% compared to fiscal 2025. Space and Defense sales increased 22% to $1.4 billion, reflecting broad-based defense demand including demand for missile controls, ground vehicles and spacecraft products. Military Aircraft sales increased 14% to $1.0 billion, driven by strong aftermarket and OEM activity, including peak levels of development on the MV-75 program. Commercial Aircraft sales increased 17% to $1.1 billion, driven by higher volume and pricing on various major production programs, as well as strong aftermarket sales. Industrial sales increased 15% to $1.1 billion, driven by strong demand for data center cooling pumps, as well as for medical applications.

Segment operating margin for fiscal 2026 was 13.9%, an increase of 230 basis points compared to fiscal 2025. Industrial operating margin increased 350 basis points to 14.8%, primarily driven by the growing data center cooling pump business, the tariff refund and lower amounts of simplification and other charges. Military Aircraft operating margin expanded 280 basis points to 13.9% driven by favorable sales mix, pricing and by the absence of the prior year’s product development termination charge. Space and Defense operating margin increased 230 basis points to 14.1% due to the absence of the prior year's legal settlement charges and due to profitable sales growth. Commercial Aircraft operating margin increased 20 basis points to 12.6%. Significant pricing benefits, the tariff refund and a gain from a non-core business sale were mostly offset by an unfavorable sales mix, a full year's worth of tariff expense and the absence of the gain on the prior year's non-core product line sale.

Adjusted segment operating margins for fiscal 2026 and 2025 exclude net charges of $17 million and $52 million, respectively. Excluding these items, adjusted segment operating margin in fiscal 2026 expanded 120 basis points to 14.2% compared to fiscal 2025. Adjusted segment operating margins in Industrial, Military Aircraft, and Space and Defense increased 250 basis points, 180 basis points and 120 basis points, respectively, while Commercial Aircraft decreased 30 basis points.

Income Tax Expense

The effective tax rate for fiscal 2026 includes income tax benefits related to U.S. federal research credits of $35 million attributable to prior years. We also recognized an income tax benefit of $8 million related to legal entity simplification initiatives. Adjusted 2026 net earnings and adjusted net earnings per share exclude both the $35 million and $8 million income tax benefits.

Free Cash Flow Results

Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 was $307 million, an increase of $179 million compared to 2025. Free cash flow improved due to higher earnings. In addition, working capital efficiency improved, as reflected in lower net working capital as a percentage of sales compared with the prior year. Capital expenditures were $136 million, relatively unchanged.

Fiscal 2027 Financial Guidance

"We had a strong finish to a record year. Our fourth quarter was marked by record sales in each of our segments, a robust operating margin and strong cash generation," said Jennifer Walter, CFO. "In fiscal year 2027, we'll continue to build upon our financial strength with record sales, stronger operating performance and meaningful operating cash flows."

Coral Gables, Florida--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Sucro Limited (TSXV: SUGR) (OTCQB: SUGRF) (“Sucro” or the “Company”), an integrated sugar trader and refiner focused primarily on serving North American sugar markets, today announced financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are in United States dollars (“U.S. $” or “$”) unless otherwise noted.

Financial Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026

  • Net income of $18.5 million for the quarter, up 20.2% from $15.4 million in the third quarter of 2025; $32.0 million year to date, compared to $29.4 million in the first nine months of 2025
  • Refinery volumes reached a record 105,614 metric tons, nearly double the 53,873 metric tons delivered in the third quarter of 2025 and the third consecutive record quarter for Sucro’s refineries
  • Revenue of $126.8 million on sugar deliveries of 147,428 metric tons, compared to $132.9 million and 147,853 metric tons, respectively, in the third quarter of 2025, as average sugar delivery prices declined to $843.50 per metric ton from $893.30
  • Adjusted gross profit1 of $13.1 million, compared to $13.4 million in the third quarter of 2025, and adjusted gross profit margin1 of 10.3%, up from 10.1%
  • Adjusted gross profit per metric ton delivered1 of $88.78, compared to $90.91 in the third quarter of 2025
  • Logistics and freight costs rose 52.6%, or $7.8 million, to $22.5 million, driven by U.S. customs duties and tariffs, higher diesel fuel prices and carrier fuel surcharges, which the Company has not been able to pass on to customers in current U.S. market conditions
  • Refinery adjusted gross profit per metric ton delivered1 of $82.45, compared to $187.66 in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting these unrecovered costs and temporary transfer costs during the ramp-up of the University Park refinery
  • Adjusted EBITDA¹ of $7.0 million, compared to $8.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, and EBITDA¹ of $27.2 million, compared to $20.8 million
  • SG&A of $10.1 million, up $1.9 million year-over-year, including a $1.6 million provision against approximately 5,000 metric tons of sugar held under warehouse receipts in Mexico that are subject to a legal dispute; interest expense decreased 12.4% to $5.0 million

“Our third quarter results reflect a challenging U.S. sugar market,” said Jonathan Taylor, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Sucro. “Sugar prices were lower, and customs duties, tariffs and a sharp increase in diesel fuel prices and carrier surcharges added cost to the sugar we delivered in the U.S. Competitive market conditions meant we were not able to pass these additional costs on to our customers, and that weighed on our refining margins. Even so, we held adjusted gross profit essentially flat year-over-year and delivered a third consecutive record quarter for refinery volumes, which speaks to the resilience of our integrated model.”

“The investments we have made in our refineries leave Sucro well positioned for 2027,” Mr. Taylor continued. “Our new Hamilton refinery is operating and steadily improving, following the consolidation of our Canadian production into that single state-of-the-art facility. University Park is now a full refinery, and together with Lackawanna it is prepared to deliver significant volumes of higher value-added organic sugar in 2027. We have also begun renegotiating delivery terms with customers to recover higher freight costs. With this expanded and more flexible refining capacity in place, we believe Sucro is ready to benefit as market conditions become more favorable in 2027.”

Results from Operations – Three Months Ended September 30, 2026

Revenue for the quarter was $126.8 million (compared to $132.9 million for the corresponding period in 2025), with sugar deliveries of 147,428 metric tons (compared to 147,853 metric tons for the corresponding period in 2025). The decrease in revenue was mainly driven by lower average sugar delivery prices of $843.50 per metric ton, compared to $893.30 per metric ton in the prior-year period, reflecting market conditions. Adjusted gross profit was $13.1 million (compared to $13.4 million for the corresponding period in 2025), representing an adjusted gross profit margin of 10.3% (compared to 10.1% for the corresponding period in 2025). Adjusted gross profit per metric ton delivered was $88.78 (compared to $90.91 for the corresponding period in 2025).

Net income for the quarter was $18.5 million (compared to $15.4 million for the corresponding period in 2025). EBITDA was $27.2 million (compared to $20.8 million for the corresponding prior period), and Adjusted EBITDA was $7.0 million (compared to $8.1 million for the corresponding prior period), with an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 5.5% compared to 6.1% for the corresponding prior period. The decrease in Adjusted EBITDA reflects higher selling, general and administrative expenses, including the $1.6 million inventory provision noted above under “Financial Highlights for the Third Quarter of 2026”.

U.S. market conditions weighed on margins during the quarter. Logistics and freight costs increased to $22.5 million from $14.8 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven predominantly by customs duties and tariffs and by higher delivery freight costs, as diesel fuel prices and related carrier fuel surcharges rose substantially in the second half of 2026. Competitive dynamics in the U.S. market limited the Company’s ability to pass these additional costs on to customers, compressing margins on certain sales. Refinery adjusted gross profit per metric ton declined to $82.45 from $187.66 in the prior-year period, which also reflects additional transportation costs associated with transferring product between facilities during the commissioning and ramp-up of the University Park refinery. During the third quarter, the Company began renegotiating delivery terms with customers to recover these additional costs.

Sucro’s refineries delivered a record 105,614 metric tons in the quarter, nearly double the 53,873 metric tons delivered in the corresponding period of 2025, and 301,919 metric tons year to date, an increase of 87.4%. These volumes reflect the ramp-up of the Company’s new Hamilton, Ontario refinery, export opportunities from Canada, and the conversion of the University Park, Illinois facility into a full refinery that also supplies a related third-party facility in Memphis. In the fourth quarter, the Company expects to decommission its legacy Hamilton refinery and consolidate its Canadian operations into the new state-of-the-art facility, which is expected to improve production and overhead costs per metric ton. The Company has also increased its organic raw sugar inventory in preparation to deliver significant volumes of organic sugar from its Lackawanna and University Park refineries in 2027, strengthening its leadership position in the U.S. organic sugar market.

The Company’s joint venture refinery in Belize, developed with Santander Sugar Limited, is expected to begin operations in the fourth quarter of 2026. The Company has discontinued its Guyana refinery project and terminated its joint venture agreement with GAICO Construction & General Services Inc.

The Company is in the process of refinancing all of its term debt relating to its U.S. facilities, including $17.5 million of loans maturing within the next 12 months, and expects to complete this process before year-end. As of September 30, 2026, the Company was in compliance with the financial covenants under its credit facilities.

Award of Restricted Share Units

The Board of Directors has awarded 18,498 restricted share units (“RSUs”) to non-executive directors as part of their annual retainer under the Company’s Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan. These RSU awards occur semi-annually in April and November of each year. The RSUs awarded will vest one year from the date of the award. All awards are subject to regulatory approval.

Q3 2026 Investor Call

The Company will host a conference call on Friday, November 20, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time during which Jonathan Taylor, Founder and Chief Executive Officer, and Stefano D’Aniello, Chief Financial Officer, will discuss Sucro’s financial performance for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Date: Friday November 20, 2026 
Time: 10:00 am ET

About Sucro

Sucro is a growth-oriented sugar trader and refiner that operates throughout the Americas, with a primary focus on serving the North American sugar market. The Company operates a highly integrated and interconnected sugar supply business, utilizing the entire sugar supply chain to service its customers. Sucro’s integrated supply chain includes sourcing raw and refined sugar from countries throughout Latin America, and refined sugar from its own refineries, and delivering to customers in North America and the Caribbean. Since its inception in 2014, Sucro has achieved growth by creating value for customers through continuous process innovation and supply chain re-engineering. Sucro has established a broad production, sales, and sourcing network throughout North America with cane sugar refineries in Hamilton, Ontario, Lackawanna, New York, and University Park, Illinois (a suburb of Chicago), additional value-added processing and packaging facilities, and a cane sugar refinery under development in Belize through a joint venture. The Company has offices in Miami, Mexico City, Cali, Sao Paulo, and Port of Spain. For more information, visit sucro.us and follow us on LinkedIn.

Driven by a seasoned management team, Fortitude pairs self-mining operations with an owned data center footprint and a controlled power portfolio to scale high conviction opportunities across the broader digital asset landscape.

AUBURN HILLS, Mich.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- PHINIA Inc. (NYSE: PHIN), a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems and aftermarket solutions, announced today the appointment of Gordon Muir as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective January 1, 2027. Muir succeeds Chris Gropp, current SVP and CFO, who will retire, effective March 31, 2027.

Gropp will support the transition period starting January 1 through March 31, 2027, as Special Advisor, also reporting to Brady Ericson, President and Chief Executive Officer, focusing on a smooth and well-coordinated transition of responsibilities.

“Gordon played a critical role in PHINIA becoming an independent company in 2023 and has continued to be an important part of our success. He has a deep understanding of our business and brings significant financial expertise, including extensive experience with complex corporate transactions and transformations,” said Brady Ericson, President and Chief Executive Officer of PHINIA. “I am pleased to welcome Gordon to PHINIA’s executive leadership team. He is highly respected across the company and well positioned to step into the CFO role next year,” continued Ericson.

“I would also like to recognize Chris for her significant contributions and dedication to PHINIA. She has played an important role in our success, supporting two acquisitions, driving strong financial performance, and helping position the business for sustainable, long-term growth. Her exceptional global corporate finance and accounting expertise has been invaluable to our organization. Personally, I want to thank Chris for her leadership, outstanding commitment, and partnership throughout this journey,” concluded Ericson.

“Being part of PHINIA’s foundation and growth path, has been an honor. Representing this Company has been an exciting journey, and I am proud to be part of its history and exceptional team,” commented Gropp.

About Gordon Muir

Gordon joined BorgWarner in 2007 and has been part of PHINIA since its spin-off in 2023. He currently serves as PHINIA's Treasurer, with responsibility for Treasury and Investor Relations, and has played a key role in the Company’s financial strategy and capital markets activities. He brings extensive global finance experience, with deep expertise in treasury, financial strategy, and corporate finance. Gordon holds a Master of Business Administration from the University of Notre Dame, a Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance and Accounting from Grand Valley State University, and attended the Advanced Management Program at Harvard Business School. In addition, Gordon is a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and Certified Public Accountant (CPA). In his new role, Gordon will build on PHINIA’s strong finance culture, bringing a disciplined approach to supporting the business and advancing the Company’s long-term strategic objectives.

About PHINIA

PHINIA is a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, with a strong portfolio of trusted brands that includes DELPHI®, DELCO REMY®, HARTRIDGE™ and stoba®. With over 100 years of manufacturing expertise and industry relationships, PHINIA has approximately 13,500 talented employees and over 40 locations in 21 countries and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA.

PHINIA’s service solutions include vehicle repair and replacement parts, offering both new and remanufactured products through the original equipment manufacturer dealer network and the independent aftermarket channel.

By delivering high-performance solutions today and investing in advanced technologies to unlock the potential of alternative fuels in contributing to lower carbon mobility, PHINIA is shaping a more efficient and sustainable future.

HOUSTON, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- IES Holdings, Inc. (or “IES” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: IESC) today announced financial results for the quarter and fiscal year ended September 30, 2026.

Fourth Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue of $1.39 billion for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of 55% compared with $898 million for the same quarter of fiscal 2025
  • Operating income of $217.2 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of 108% compared with $104.3 million for the same quarter of fiscal 2025
  • Net income attributable to IES of $182.3 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of 79% compared with $101.8 million for the same quarter of fiscal 2025, and diluted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders of $4.50 for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $2.49 for the same quarter of fiscal 2025
  • Adjusted net income attributable to IES (a non-GAAP financial measure, as defined below) of $165.1 million for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of 114% compared with $77.0 million for the same quarter of fiscal 2025, and diluted adjusted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders of $4.07 for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with $1.88 for the same quarter of fiscal 2025
  • Remaining performance obligations, a GAAP measure of future revenue to be recognized from current contracts with customers, of approximately $3.48 billion as of September 30, 2026
  • Backlog (a non-GAAP financial measure, as defined below) of approximately $4.96 billion as of September 30, 2026
  • Subsequent to quarter end, on October 5, 2026, completed the acquisition of DBM Global, adding a new Structural line of business and expanded our credit facility from $300 million to $700 million
  • Subsequent to quarter end, our Board of Directors authorized an additional $350 million for our share repurchase program

Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue of $4.48 billion for fiscal 2026, an increase of 33% compared with $3.37 billion for fiscal 2025
  • Operating income of $605.7 million for fiscal 2026, an increase of 58% compared with $383.5 million for fiscal 2025
  • Net income attributable to IES of $536.6 million for fiscal 2026, an increase of 75% compared with $306.0 million for fiscal 2025, and diluted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders of $13.24 for fiscal 2026, compared with $7.51 for fiscal 2025
  • Adjusted net income attributable to IES of $459.8 million for fiscal 2026, an increase of 66% compared with $277.8 million for fiscal 2025, and diluted adjusted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders of $11.34 for fiscal 2026 compared with $6.81 for fiscal 2025

Overview of Results

“We are pleased to report outstanding operating performance, resulting in record earnings for fiscal year 2026," said Matt Simmes, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Year-over-year consolidated revenue increased 33% and operating income increased 58%, driven by strong execution by our operating teams, our continued investment in growth, and the strength of the key markets in which we operate. I also want to recognize our teams for their focus on continuous improvement in safety over the year, reinforcing our commitment to a strong safety culture across the organization. With record levels of backlog at September 30, 2026, we expect continued strong organic growth in fiscal 2027 in our Communications, Commercial & Industrial and Infrastructure Solutions segments.” 

"In October 2026 we completed our acquisition of DBM Global, establishing a new Structural line of business. We are excited about the addition of DBM Global's engineering, fabrication and erection capabilities and approximately 4,000 skilled employees to the IES team. The addition of DBM Global broadens the range of products and services we offer our customers, and we are optimistic about the new business opportunities that its skilled workforce and over two million square feet of operating facilities will enable in fiscal 2027. This acquisition also added backlog of $2.6 billion, which is not included in our September 30, 2026 backlog amounts described above.”

Our Communications segment’s revenue was $1.69 billion in fiscal 2026, an increase of 48% compared with fiscal 2025, driven by investments we have made in the business to keep pace with the continuously increasing demand from our customers in the data center end market. The segment's operating income increased to $290.0 million for fiscal 2026, compared with $166.5 million for fiscal 2025, as we benefited from strong project execution, our ability to scale effectively, and strong market conditions.

Our Commercial & Industrial segment’s revenue was $799.5 million in fiscal 2026, an increase of 83% compared with fiscal 2025. The increase in revenue was primarily driven by continued strong demand and successful execution in the data center end market, as we benefited from our efforts to expand our capabilities and trained workforce in that space. Segment operating income for fiscal 2026 was $163.1 million, compared with $47.3 million for fiscal 2025. Our operating margins, particularly in the second half of fiscal 2026, benefited from some large, quick-turning projects we executed at favorable margins, and our teams rose to the challenge of executing these projects successfully.

Our Infrastructure Solutions segment’s revenue was $826.6 million in fiscal 2026, an increase of 66% compared with fiscal 2025, driven by continued strong demand in our custom engineered solutions business, primarily for the data center end market, where investments we have made in capacity over the past several years have enabled us to meet customer demand. Operating income for fiscal 2026 was $194.4 million, compared with $118.5 million for fiscal 2025. The year-over-year profit improvement was driven by higher volumes and improved pricing. Operating income as a percent of revenue decreased year over year, as we continue to invest in our more recent acquisitions, which typically come on line at a lower margin than more mature facilities. However, this impact was largely mitigated by our ability to efficiently scale fixed costs as we grow. Gulf Island, which we acquired in January 2026, contributed $151 million of revenue and $11 million of operating income for the fiscal year.

Our Residential segment’s revenue was $1.22 billion in fiscal 2026, a decrease of 7% compared with fiscal 2025, reflecting weak demand in the housing market, which continues to be affected by housing affordability challenges, elevated mortgage rates, availability and cost of insurance, and overall economic uncertainty. However, the impact of these factors was partly offset by continued expansion of our plumbing and HVAC trades into new geographic markets. As the cost of inputs rose throughout fiscal 2026, weak demand limited our ability to recover cost increases through pricing actions in our single-family business. In our multi-family business, lower revenue year-over-year reflects the impacts of prolonged elevated borrowing costs for project owners, which resulted in lower backlog entering fiscal 2026. As a result of these factors, the Residential segment’s operating income was $40.1 million for fiscal 2026, compared with $103.8 million for fiscal 2025.

“As we look forward to fiscal 2027, we are optimistic about our outlook for continued strong performance based on our existing and recently added operating capabilities and capacity, in combination with the favorable environment in many of the industries we serve, and we intend to continue aggressive pursuit of organic growth and selective acquisitions," said Jeff Gendell, Executive Chairman. "We structured our financing of the DBM Global acquisition intentionally, balancing the use of cash, equity and borrowings under our credit facility to provide flexibility for future opportunities to grow our business. Subsequent to our fiscal 2026 year end, we took advantage of the stock market disruptions impacting trading prices in our industry to repurchase 350,000 shares of our common stock at an average price of $248.00, substantially mitigating the dilutive impact of the shares issued as part of the consideration for the purchase of DBM Global. On November 19, our Board of Directors authorized an additional $350 million for our share repurchase program.”

Capital Allocation; Stock Buyback Plan

"We ended the year with $155.1 million of cash, $288.9 million of marketable securities and no debt, positioning us advantageously to complete our acquisition of DBM Global after the close of the fiscal year," added Tracy McLauchlin, Chief Financial Officer. "On October 5, 2026, in connection with that transaction, we expanded our credit facility from $300 million to $700 million, and borrowed $525 million to fund the acquisition. Through November 19, 2026, we have repaid $125 million of that borrowing. We expect strong operating cash flow generation from the business in fiscal 2027, which we will use to repay debt and fund capital expenditures to support continued growth, maintaining flexibility for other capital allocation priorities."

Capital allocation highlights during fiscal 2026 include the following:

  • We invested $143.1 million to acquire Gulf Island
  • We supported the growth of our operating businesses with $163.1 million in capital expenditures
  • We repurchased 26,465 shares of our common stock for $7.2 million, or an average price of $270.59 per share, ending the year with $160.8 million remaining under our stock repurchase authorization
  • We used $245.3 million of our excess cash to purchase marketable securities

Capital allocation highlights subsequent to the end of the fiscal year include:

  • On October 5, 2026, we expanded our credit facility from $300 million to $700 million and borrowed $525 million to fund our acquisition of DBM Global
  • Through November 19, 2026, we repurchased an additional 350,000 shares of our common stock for $86.8 million, or an average price of $248.00 per share
  • On November 19, 2026, our Board of Directors approved an additional $350 million for our stock repurchase program

Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Adjustments

This press release includes adjusted net income attributable to IES, adjusted diluted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders, and backlog, and, in the non-GAAP reconciliation tables included herein, adjusted net income attributable to common stockholders, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted income from operations before income taxes, each of which is a financial measure not calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the U.S. (“GAAP”). Management believes that these measures provide useful information to our investors by, in the case of adjusted net income attributable to IES, adjusted net income attributable to common stockholders, adjusted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted income from operations before income taxes, distinguishing certain nonrecurring events such as litigation settlements, significant expenses associated with leadership changes, or gains or losses from the sale of a business, noncash events, such as impairment charges, items that are not indicative of quarterly business performance such as gains and losses on our investments, or, in the case of backlog, providing a common measurement used in IES's industry, as described further below, and that these measures, when reconciled to the most directly comparable GAAP measures, help our investors to better identify underlying trends in the operations of our business and facilitate easier comparisons of our financial performance with prior and future periods and to our peers. Non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, financial information calculated in accordance with GAAP. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, which has been provided in the financial tables included in this press release.

Remaining performance obligations represent the unrecognized revenue value of our contract commitments. While backlog is not a defined term under GAAP, it is a common measurement used in IES’s industry and IES believes this non-GAAP measure enables it to more effectively forecast its future results and better identify future operating trends that may not otherwise be apparent. IES’s remaining performance obligations are a component of IES’s backlog calculation, which also includes signed agreements and letters of intent which we do not have a legal right to enforce prior to work starting. These arrangements are excluded from remaining performance obligations until work begins. IES’s methodology for determining backlog may not be comparable to the methodologies used by other companies.

Common Shares to Trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market Under the Symbol “CZZL”

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cizzle Brands Corporation (Cboe Canada: CZZL; OTCQB: CZZLF; Frankfurt: 8YF) (“Cizzle Brands” or the “Company”), the sports nutrition company that is elevating the game in health and wellness, today announced the pricing of its underwritten public offering (the “Offering”) in connection with the uplisting of its common shares to the Nasdaq Capital Market. The Company is offering 3,030,000 common shares at a public offering price of US$5.00 per share. The Company has also granted the Underwriter (as defined below) a 45-day option to purchase up to an additional 454,500 common shares, representing 15% of the common shares sold in the Offering. The common shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market on November 20, 2026 under the symbol “CZZL.”

The gross proceeds from the Offering, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other estimated Offering expenses payable by the Company, are expected to be approximately US$15.15 million, excluding any exercise of the Underwriter’s option to purchase additional shares. The Offering is expected to close on or about November 23, 2026, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for repayment of a portion of the indebtedness incurred to finance its acquisition of Flow Water Inc.’s beverage co-manufacturing business; capital expenditures to expand production capacity at The CWENCH Hydration Factory in Aurora, Ontario, including additional Tetra Pak aseptic filling and packaging capacity and related plant and equipment; and general corporate purposes, including ongoing operations, working capital and growth initiatives. However, the Company’s management will have broad discretion with respect to the actual use of the net proceeds from the Offering.

Joseph Gunnar & Co., LLC (the “Underwriter”) is acting as sole book-running manager for the Offering. Research Capital Corporation is acting as an agent for the sale of common shares in the Offering in Canada.

A registration statement on Form F-10 (File No. 333-298427) related to the Offering of the common shares described above was filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) and became effective on September 29, 2026 pursuant to Rule 467(b) under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended. A copy of the registration statement can be accessed by visiting the SEC website at www.sec.gov. The common shares are being offered and sold in the United States only by means of a prospectus supplement and the accompanying short form base shelf prospectus dated October 7, 2025, forming part of the registration statement. A final prospectus supplement relating to this Offering will be filed with the SEC. When available, a copy of the final prospectus supplement and accompanying base shelf prospectus may be obtained from Joseph Gunnar & Co., LLC, Prospectus Department, 40 Wall Street, 30th Floor, New York, NY 10005, telephone 212-440-9600, email: prospectus@jgunnar.com Investors may also obtain these documents at no cost by visiting the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov and under the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

Before you invest, you should read the prospectus and other documents the Company has filed or will file with the SEC for more complete information about the Company and the Offering.

As previously disclosed, a portion of the Offering is being raised in Canada in reliance on the “listed issuer financing” exemption from the prospectus requirements available under Part 5A.2 of National Instrument 45-106 - Prospectus Exemptions, as modified by Coordinated Blanket Order 45-935 - Exemptions from Certain Conditions of the Listed Issuer Financing Exemption (the “Listed Issuer Financing Exemption”). An amended and restated offering document containing final pricing for the Offering (the “Offering Document”) can be accessed in English and French under the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company’s website at www.cizzlebrands.com. Prospective investors in Canada should read the Offering Document before making an investment decision concerning the common shares. Any distribution of common shares outside of Canada will be made pursuant to applicable foreign securities laws and the public offering exemption available under BC Instrument 72‑503 – Distribution of Securities outside British Columbia.

The Company also confirms that the consolidation of its outstanding common shares on the basis of one (1) post-consolidation common share for every twenty-five (25) pre-consolidation common shares (the “Consolidation”) has taken effect as of November 20, 2026. Trading of the post-Consolidation common shares on Nasdaq and Cboe Canada is expected to commence on November 20, 2026 under the existing symbol “CZZL.” The Company’s common shares will trade under a new CUSIP number (17888V201) and ISIN (CA17888V2012). The exercise price and the number of common shares issuable under the Company’s outstanding warrants and options will be proportionately adjusted to reflect the Consolidation. Fractional shares created as a result of the Consolidation will be rounded down to the nearest whole share.

Following the Consolidation and assuming no additional issuances, the Company expects to have approximately 9,217,365 common shares issued and outstanding, prior to rounding for fractional shares and prior to giving effect to the Offering.

In connection with the Consolidation, the Company will not require a letter of transmittal from holders of common shares whose shares are held in book-entry or DRS form. All such shareholders will automatically receive the post-Consolidation Shares to which they are entitled, and Odyssey Trust Company, as transfer agent, will distribute the applicable DRS statements. Odyssey Trust Company has confirmed that all common shares of the Company held by registered shareholders as of the effective date on November 20, 2026 will be processed. The Consolidation remains subject to the policies of Cboe Canada.

The Company also announced that it intends to extend the expiry date of 36,419,635 outstanding common share purchase warrants (on a pre-Consolidation basis) that are currently scheduled to expire at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on November 28, 2026 (the “Warrants”) by 12 months, to November 28, 2027 (the “Warrant Extension”). The Warrants were originally scheduled to expire on August 28, 2026, and their expiry date was previously extended to November 28, 2026. All other terms of the Warrants, including the exercise price of $0.40 per share (on a pre-Consolidation basis, subject to adjustment in accordance with their terms, including for the Consolidation) and the Company’s right to accelerate the expiry date, will remain unchanged. The Warrant Extension has been approved by written resolution of disinterested shareholders in accordance with the policies of Cboe Canada and remains subject to acceptance by Cboe Canada.

About Cizzle Brands Corporation

Cizzle Brands Corporation is a vertically integrated sports nutrition company that is elevating the game in health and wellness. Through extensive collaboration and testing with leading athletes and trainers across several sports, Cizzle Brands has launched three game-changing brands: (i) CWENCH Hydration™, a better-for-you sports drink that is now carried in over 6,900 locations in Canada, the United States, and Europe; (ii) Spoken™ Nutrition, a premium brand of athlete-grade nutraceuticals that carry the prestigious NSF Certified for Sport® qualification; and (iii) HappiEats™, upgrading everyday eats with high-performance foods such as Sport Pasta™ and SnakStars™ Sport Bites. It also owns and operates The CWENCH Hydration Factory, a manufacturing facility that produces CWENCH Hydration and other leading beverage brands in Tetra Pak packaging. All Cizzle Brands products are designed to help people of all ages achieve their best in competitive sports and in living a healthy, vibrant, active lifestyle.

TORONTO, ON / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / COLLECTIVE METALS INC. (CSE:COMT)(OTC PINK:CLLMF)(FSE:TO1) (the "Company" or "Collective Metals") announces that it has entered into an option agreement (the "Agreement") with an arm's length vendor (the "Vendor"), under which the Company may acquire a 100% interest in the Lac Tio West Property (the "Property") from the Vendor. The Property consists of 56 contiguous mineral claims totalling approximately 3,062 hectares in the Minganie region of the Côte-Nord, Quebec, and adjoins mining titles held by Rio Tinto Fer et Titane inc. around its Lac Tio ilmenite mine near Havre-Saint-Pierre.

Under the Agreement, the Company may acquire a 100% interest in the Property by:

  • paying the Vendor $100,000 in cash on the Effective Date (defined below) and $50,000 on each of the first, second and third anniversaries of the Effective Date, being $250,000 in total;
  • issuing to the Vendor, on the Effective Date, common shares equal to 9.9% of the Company's issued and outstanding common shares immediately following the issuance, and on each of the first, second and third anniversaries such additional shares as are required to bring the aggregate number of shares issued to the Vendor under the Agreement to 9.9% of the issued and outstanding common shares; and
  • incurring exploration expenditures on the Property of $100,000 by the first anniversary, a further $150,000 by the second anniversary and a further $200,000 by the third anniversary of the Effective Date, being $450,000 in total.

Any shortfall in exploration expenditures at an anniversary is payable to the Vendor in cash or, at the Company's election, in common shares, subject to CSE acceptance. The Vendor retains no royalty. The Company will act as operator. The "Effective Date" is the date on which the CSE accepts the Agreement for filing. All shares issued under the Agreement will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

Mineralization at the Lac Tio mine is not necessarily indicative of mineralization on the Property.

The Company has decided not to proceed with its option to acquire a 75% interest in the Rocas uranium project in Saskatchewan (the "Project"). The option was granted under a property option agreement dated September 26, 2025 (the "Option Agreement") with Standard Uranium Ltd. and Standard Uranium (Saskatchewan) Ltd. (together, "Standard Uranium"). The Project comprises approximately 4,002 hectares in the eastern Athabasca Basin region. The Company has not earned an ownership interest in the Project and will not pursue the remaining earn-in requirements under the Option Agreement.
